title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon AI model, rivals Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol
summary: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon AI model, rivaling Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol
detailed: Google has launched Gemini 4 Neon, a model they say brings frontier-level intelligence to the realms of complex coding, knowledge work, and science work without the long wait.
If you're paying for Google AI Pro or Ultra, you can now select Neon from the model menu in the Gemini app too.

sentences: Google has launched Gemini 4 Neon, a model they say brings frontier-level intelligence to the realms of complex coding, knowledge work, and science work without the long wait.
If you're paying for Google AI Pro or Ultra, you can now select Neon from the model menu in the Gemini app too.
When I went into the app, it was immediately apparent that Neon has taken the place of Argon in the model picker.
It's now under the 'Deeper analysis' heading, with Hydrogen under 'Everyday help'.
The naming scheme for these new models is a complete mess, so let's break that down first.
Neon sits between Gemini 4 Carbon, which Google keeps for the most difficult long-horizon projects, and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the faster, more everyday model.
API pricing is $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens (with cached input at $0.15).
The context window is 1 million tokens.
It has four thinking levels, with 'high' as the default.
"To me Neon feels like the right mix of intelligence, speed and usability," wrote Logan Kilpatrick in a post.

"It's absolutely punching well above its model class in a meaningful way."
Introducing Gemini 4 Neon!
Pushing the frontier across domains and punching above its model class in a meaningful way.
To me, Neon feels like the right balance of intelligence, speed, and usability.

Available now across @GoogleAIStudio, the API, and more! pic.twitter.com/ANqCSTEWcS
Google's own comparison table puts Neon ahead of both Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (score 61 v 59 v 57).
Google states that 61 puts Neon in third place overall, behind the bigger, slower models.
Neon comes out on top on the Vals Index (70.9%) and on AutomationBench (56.3%).
It is behind Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and FrontierCode 2.0, and behind GPT-6.2 Sol on Chartography.
At its default 'high thinking' level, Neon is effectively on par with Carbon on the same index, at 32% lower cost per task and 50-80% less per task than the leading frontier models.
In the Gemini app, Google says Neon is for writing, for research, and for all the messy day-to-day stuff like reading a pile of receipts or checking your utility bill.
It can work across spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio, and video all in one prompt.
Those are Google's own benchmarks, so independent tests may well come out differently.
